entries.summary: Anthropic Python SDK v0.20+ migrated from the legacy Completions API to the Messages API, changing the primary client interface and method signatures.

changes.before:
import anthropic
client = anthropic.Client("sk-ant-...")
response = client.completions.create(
    model="claude-2",
    prompt=f"{anthropic.HUMAN_PROMPT}Hello{anthropic.AI_PROMPT}",
    max_tokens_to_sample=100,
)
text = response.completion
changes.after:
from anthropic import Anthropic
client = Anthropic()
response = client.messages.create(
    model="claude-3-5-sonnet-20241022",
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Hello"}],
    max_tokens=100,
)
text = response.content[0].text
changes.migration_note: The Completions API (using HUMAN_PROMPT/AI_PROMPT) was replaced by the Messages API. Use client.messages.create() with messages array. max_tokens_to_sample renamed to max_tokens. Response structure changed from response.completion to response.content[0].text.

changes.before:
import anthropic
prompt = f"{anthropic.HUMAN_PROMPT}What is 2+2?{anthropic.AI_PROMPT}"
changes.after:
from anthropic import Anthropic
messages = [{"role": "user", "content": "What is 2+2?"}]
changes.migration_note: HUMAN_PROMPT and AI_PROMPT constants removed. Use the messages list format with role/content dictionaries.

changes.before:
import anthropic
client = anthropic.Client("sk-ant-...")
changes.after:
from anthropic import Anthropic
client = Anthropic()
changes.migration_note: Client class renamed to Anthropic. API key now read from ANTHROPIC_API_KEY env var by default.

entries.summary: ChromaDB Python SDK breaking changes from 0.4.0 through 1.0.0, covering client constructor overhaul, removed persist()/reset() defaults, generic EmbeddingFunction signature, auth system rewrite, result ordering/type changes, filter semantics, and the 1.0.0 Rust rewrite.

changes.before: client = chromadb.Client(Settings(chroma_db_impl="duckdb+parquet", persist_directory="/path/to/data"))
changes.after: client = chromadb.PersistentClient(path="/path/to/data")
changes.migration_note: The old client construction pattern using Settings(chroma_db_impl=...) was removed in 0.4.0, which dropped duckdb/clickhouse in favor of sqlite for metadata storage. Existing data must be migrated via `pip install chroma-migrate && chroma-migrate`. The new dedicated client constructors (PersistentClient, EphemeralClient, HttpClient) replace the generic Client(Settings(...)) for storage backends.

changes.before: client = chromadb.Client()  # in-memory ephemeral client
changes.after: client = chromadb.EphemeralClient()
changes.migration_note: The bare chromadb.Client() no longer creates the in-memory ephemeral client in the same way. The recommended replacement is chromadb.EphemeralClient(). The underlying .Client() remains accessible but the previous default behavior changed.

changes.before: client = chromadb.Client(Settings(chroma_api_impl="rest", chroma_server_host="localhost", chroma_server_http_port="8000"))
changes.after: client = chromadb.HttpClient(host="localhost", port="8000")
changes.migration_note: The HTTP/REST client construction via Settings(chroma_api_impl="rest", ...) was replaced by the dedicated HttpClient(host=..., port=...) constructor.

changes.before: client.persist()  # or collection.persist()
changes.after: # (removed — no replacement needed)
changes.migration_note: .persist() existed in old versions because writes were only flushed when forced. In 0.4.0, Chroma saves all writes to disk instantly, so .persist() is no longer needed and was removed. Calling it now raises AttributeError.

changes.before: client.reset()  # enabled by default
changes.after: client = chromadb.PersistentClient(path="./data", settings=Settings(allow_reset=True))  # reset disabled unless explicitly enabled
changes.migration_note: .reset() (which wipes the entire database) used to be enabled by default. In 0.4.0 it is disabled by default and must be explicitly enabled by passing allow_reset=True to a Settings object. Existing code that calls client.reset() without the setting will now fail.

changes.symbol_before: class EmbeddingFunction(Protocol): def __call__(self, texts: Documents) -> Embeddings
changes.symbol_after: class EmbeddingFunction(Protocol[D]): def __call__(self, input: D) -> Embeddings
changes.migration_note: EmbeddingFunction became generic (takes type parameter D) to support multi-modal embeddings. The __call__ argument was renamed from `texts` to `input`, and the `texts` argument was removed. Custom EmbeddingFunction implementations must rename the parameter and update their signature. Users of built-in embedding functions are unaffected.

changes.before:
CHROMA_SERVER_AUTH_PROVIDER="chromadb.auth.token.TokenAuthServerProvider"
CHROMA_SERVER_AUTH_CREDENTIALS_PROVIDER="chromadb.auth.token.TokenConfigServerAuthCredentialsProvider"
CHROMA_SERVER_AUTH_CREDENTIALS="test-token"
CHROMA_CLIENT_AUTH_PROVIDER="chromadb.auth.token.TokenAuthClientProvider"
CHROMA_CLIENT_AUTH_CREDENTIALS="test-token"
changes.after:
CHROMA_SERVER_AUTHN_PROVIDER="chromadb.auth.token_authn.TokenAuthenticationServerProvider"
CHROMA_SERVER_AUTHN_CREDENTIALS="test-token"
CHROMA_CLIENT_AUTH_PROVIDER="chromadb.auth.token_authn.TokenAuthClientProvider"
CHROMA_CLIENT_AUTH_CREDENTIALS="test-token"
changes.migration_note: The auth system was overhauled. Many config settings were renamed or deleted: chroma_server_auth_provider -> chroma_server_authn_provider (renamed); chroma_client_auth_credentials_provider, chroma_client_auth_protocol_adapter, chroma_client_auth_credentials_file (deleted — folded into chroma_client_auth_provider / chroma_client_auth_credentials); chroma_server_auth_credentials -> chroma_server_authn_credentials (renamed); chroma_server_auth_token_transport_header / chroma_client_auth_token_transport_header -> chroma_auth_token_transport_header (renamed/merged). Custom auth/authorization provider implementations must be updated to the new ClientAuthProvider / ServerAuthenticationProvider / ServerAuthorizationProvider classes.

changes.before: size = client.max_batch_size  # property access
changes.after: size = client.get_max_batch_size()  # method call (may block / make HTTP request)
changes.migration_note: The Python client's max_batch_size property was removed and replaced by the get_max_batch_size() method. The change clarifies that this may be a blocking operation (the first invocation makes an HTTP request). Code reading the property attribute will now raise AttributeError.

changes.symbol_before: collection.get(limit=2, offset=2)["ids"]  # ordered by user-provided IDs
changes.symbol_after: collection.get(limit=2, offset=2)["ids"]  # ordered by internal IDs
changes.before:
results = collection.get(limit=2, offset=2)["ids"]
# returned ids ordered by user-provided IDs, e.g. ["2", "3"]
changes.after:
results = collection.get(limit=2, offset=2)["ids"]
# now returns ids ordered by internal IDs, e.g. ["1", "0"]
changes.migration_note: Results returned by collection.get() are now ordered by internal IDs instead of user-provided IDs. Because limit/offset depend on result ordering, pagination behavior changed: the same limit/offset values now return different records. The previous ordering was never explicitly documented.

changes.before:
collection = client.get_or_create_collection(name="my_coll", metadata={"version": 2})
# if collection existed, its metadata was OVERWRITTEN with the new values
changes.after:
collection = client.get_or_create_collection(name="my_coll", metadata={"version": 2})
# if collection exists, the existing collection is returned; metadata (and all other extra args) are IGNORED
changes.migration_note: get_or_create_collection behavior changed when a collection already exists and metadata is supplied. Previously the existing collection's metadata was overwritten; now the existing collection is returned as-is and all additional arguments (including metadata) are silently ignored. Code relying on metadata being updated via get_or_create must now use modify() instead.

changes.before:
result = collection.get()
# result["embeddings"] was a Python list of lists, e.g. [[0.1, 0.2, ...], ...]
changes.after:
result = collection.get()
# result["embeddings"] is now a 2-dimensional NumPy array (np.ndarray of shape (n, dim))
changes.migration_note: Embeddings returned by collection.get(), collection.query(), and collection.peek() are now 2-dimensional NumPy arrays instead of Python lists. If a request returns multiple embeddings the result is a Python list whose items are each 2D NumPy arrays. Code that assumes list-of-lists (e.g. len(result['embeddings'][0]) for dimension, or JSON-serializing directly) may break. Adding embeddings still accepts either Python lists or NumPy arrays.

changes.symbol_before: collection.get(where={"status": {"$ne": "done"}})  # $ne matches only records WITH the key
changes.symbol_after: collection.get(where={"status": {"$ne": "done"}})  # $ne also matches records WITHOUT the key
changes.before:
collection.get(where={"status": {"$ne": "done"}})
# $ne matched ONLY records that HAD the "status" key (with value != "done")
changes.after:
collection.get(where={"status": {"$ne": "done"}})
# $ne now ALSO matches records that do NOT have the "status" key at all
changes.migration_note: The $ne (not equal) and $nin (not in) operators in where clauses changed to match the complement set — the exact opposite of $eq and $in respectively. Previously they only matched records that possessed the specified key; now they also match records lacking the key entirely. The same change applies to $not_contains in where_document clauses (now matches records without a document field). Existing filters will return MORE results than before.

changes.before: collection.get(ids=["id1", "id2", "id3"], where={})  # empty where dict
changes.after: collection.get(ids=["id1", "id2", "id3"])  # omit empty where/where_document
changes.migration_note: Chroma no longer supports sending empty lists or dictionaries for metadata filtering (where), ID filtering, and similar operations. Passing where={} or where_document={} now raises an error. The empty filter must simply be omitted.

changes.symbol_before: collections = client.list_collections()  # list of Collection objects; c.name worked
changes.symbol_after: collection_names = client.list_collections()  # list of name strings
changes.after:
collection_names = client.list_collections()  # returns list of collection name strings
ef = OpenAIEmbeddingFunction(...)
collections = [client.get_collection(name=n, embedding_function=ef) for n in collection_names]
changes.migration_note: list_collections() changed from returning a list of Collection objects to returning only collection names (strings). This was done because returning Collection objects could error when collections were created with a custom (non-default) embedding function. Code that accessed .name or other attributes on the returned items will break. NOTE: this was reverted in v1.0.0 (list_collections again returns Collection objects).

changes.symbol_after: # chromadb 0.6.0+ requires Python 3.9 or higher; Python 3.8 dropped
changes.before: # chromadb 0.5.x supported Python 3.8+
changes.after: # chromadb 0.6.0+ requires Python 3.9 or higher; Python 3.8 dropped
changes.migration_note: Support for Python 3.8 was dropped in 0.6.0. Environments still on Python 3.8 cannot install chromadb >= 0.6.0.

changes.symbol_before: # Built-in auth providers (chromadb.auth.token_authn.TokenAuthClientProvider, BasicAuthClientProvider) shipped with SDK
changes.symbol_after: # No built-in auth; use HttpClient headers= or custom provider
changes.before: # Built-in authentication providers (e.g. chromadb.auth.token_authn.TokenAuthClientProvider, BasicAuthClientProvider) shipped with the SDK
changes.after: # Chroma no longer provides built-in authentication implementations; users must implement their own auth provider or use the HttpClient headers= parameter
changes.migration_note: Chroma 1.0.0 no longer provides built-in authentication implementations. Users relying on the bundled token/basic auth providers must supply auth via HttpClient headers (e.g. headers={"Authorization": "Bearer ..."}) or implement a custom provider. This is a rewrite of much of Chroma in Rust.

changes.symbol_after: collections = client.list_collections()  # now returns Collection objects again
changes.before: # list_collections() returned collection name strings (in 0.6.x)
changes.after: collections = client.list_collections()  # now returns Collection objects again
changes.migration_note: In 1.0.0, list_collections reverts to returning Collection objects (undoing the 0.6.0 change that returned name strings). Code written for 0.6.x that treats the return value as a list of strings will need to be updated to handle Collection objects.

changes.symbol_after: docker run -v ./chroma:/data chroma-core/chroma  # data now at /data
changes.before: docker run -p 8000:8000 -v ./chroma:/chroma/chroma chroma-core/chroma  # data at /chroma/chroma
changes.after: docker run -p 8000:8000 -v ./chroma:/data chroma-core/chroma  # data now at /data
changes.migration_note: The default data location in the Docker container changed from /chroma/chroma to /data. Existing volume mounts must be updated to the new path or data will not be found. Additionally, server settings previously passed via environment variables (CHROMA_SERVER_CORS_ALLOW_ORIGINS, CHROMA_OTEL_COLLECTION_ENDPOINT) are now provided via a YAML config file: `chroma run --config ./config.yaml`.

entries.summary: Cohere Python SDK v5.0.0 migrates to API v2: the v2 surface is exposed via a new ClientV2 class, chat collapses preamble/chat_history/message into messages, the Generate API is deprecated, streaming events are redesigned, many methods and parameters are removed, and tools move to JSON Schema.

changes.before:
import cohere
co = cohere.Client(api_key="<YOUR API KEY>")
changes.after:
import cohere
co = cohere.ClientV2(api_key="<YOUR API KEY>")
changes.migration_note: The v2 API surface is exposed through a new ClientV2 class rather than the v1 Client class. The old Client class still exists for v1 compatibility, but all new v2 features (messages-based chat, tool-call IDs, JSON-Schema tools) require ClientV2. This is the single most impactful change when migrating from API v1 to v2.

changes.before:
res = co_v1.chat(
    model="command-a-03-2025",
    preamble="You respond in concise sentences.",
    chat_history=[
        {"role": "user", "message": "Hello"},
        {"role": "chatbot", "message": "Hi, how can I help you today?"},
    ],
    message="I'm joining a new startup called Co1t today.",
)
changes.after:
res = co_v2.chat(
    model="command-a-plus-05-2026",
    messages=[
        {"role": "system", "content": "You respond in concise sentences."},
        {"role": "user", "content": "Hello"},
        {"role": "assistant", "content": "Hi, how can I help you today?"},
        {"role": "user", "content": "I'm joining a new startup called Co1t today."},
    ],
)
changes.migration_note: The v1 chat signature used three separate parameters — preamble, chat_history, and message. In v2 these collapse into a single messages list. The preamble becomes a system-role message; the per-message "message" key becomes "content"; and the "chatbot" role is renamed to "assistant". The top-level message= kwarg is removed entirely.

changes.before:
res = co_v1.chat(model="command-a-03-2025", message="What is 2 + 2")
print(res.text)
changes.after:
res = co_v2.chat(
    model="command-a-plus-05-2026",
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "What is 2 + 2"}],
)
print(res.message.content[0].text)
changes.migration_note: Chat response access path changed. v1 exposed the generated text directly as res.text. v2 nests it under res.message.content[0].text because a chat response can contain multiple content blocks (text, tool calls, etc.). Any code that reads .text off the response object breaks.

Streaming events were redesigned. The discriminator moved from chunk.event_type to chunk.type, the text-generation event was renamed from "text-generation" to "content-delta", and the streamed text moved from chunk.text to chunk.delta.message.content.text. v2 stream chunks are also falsy for non-content events, so a truthiness guard (if chunk:) is recommended.

changes.before: res = co_v1.chat(model=..., message=..., streaming=True)
changes.after: stream = co.chat_stream(message="...")  # streaming param injected automatically
changes.migration_note: The boolean streaming parameter on chat and generate was removed in SDK v5.0.0. To stream, call the dedicated chat_stream (or generate_stream) method instead; these methods inject the streaming flag automatically. Passing streaming=True to chat/generate now raises an error.

changes.before: co.check_api_key()
changes.after: # no direct replacement — call any endpoint; a 401 response indicates an invalid key
changes.migration_note: SDK v5.0.0 removed a large set of methods outright. check_api_key is gone with no replacement. Also removed: loglikelihood, batch_generate, codebook, batch_tokenize, batch_detokenize, detect_language, generate_feedback, generate_preference_feedback, create_cluster_job, get_cluster_job, list_cluster_jobs, wait_for_cluster_job, create_custom_model, wait_for_custom_model, get_custom_model, get_custom_model_by_name, get_custom_model_metrics, list_custom_models. Any code calling these now fails with AttributeError.

changes.before: co.generate(prompt="Write me three bullet points for my resume")
changes.after:
co.chat(
    model="command-a-03-2025",
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Write me three bullet points for my resume"}],
)
changes.migration_note: The Generate API endpoint is deprecated (slated for shutdown Aug 26, 2025 per Cohere). co.generate(prompt=...) is replaced by co.chat(...) using the messages list. The prompt parameter has no v2 equivalent — its content moves into a user-role message's content. Several Generate-only parameters (num_generations, stop_sequences, end_sequences, logit_bias, truncate, preset) are not supported by Chat at all.

Tool/function definitions moved from Cohere's bespoke parameter_definitions format to standard JSON Schema. The top-level dict must now wrap fields under a nested "function" object with "type": "function"; parameter_definitions becomes parameters; Python-style "type": "str" becomes JSON-Schema "type": "string"; and the per-field "required": True boolean is replaced by a schema-level "required": ["location"] array. Tool functions must also now return a list of objects rather than a single object.

changes.before:
res_v1 = co_v1.chat(model=..., message="What's the weather in Toronto?", tools=tools_v1)
print(res_v1.tool_calls)
# [ToolCall(name='get_weather', parameters={'location': 'Toronto'})]
changes.after:
res_v2 = co_v2.chat(model=..., messages=messages, tools=tools_v2)
print(res_v2.message.tool_calls)
# [ToolCallV2(id='get_weather_k88p0m8504w5', type='function', function=ToolCallV2Function(name='get_weather', arguments='{"location":"Toronto"}'))]
changes.migration_note: Tool calls moved from response.tool_calls to response.message.tool_calls. The tool-call object itself changed shape: v1 exposed tc.name and tc.parameters (a dict); v2 exposes tc.id, tc.type, and tc.function.name / tc.function.arguments (arguments is a JSON string, requiring json.loads). v2 also introduces tool-call IDs (tc.id) that must be echoed back as tool_call_id when returning tool results.

changes.before:
# v5.1.x: tokenize used the hosted tokenizer; model was optional
co.tokenize(text="hello world")
changes.after:
# v5.2.0+: local tokenizer is the default; model is required
co.tokenize(model="command-a-03-2025", text="hello world")
# pass offline=False to revert to the hosted tokenizer
co.tokenize(model="command-a-03-2025", text="hello world", offline=False)
changes.migration_note: In SDK v5.2.0 the tokenize and detokenize functions switched their default tokenizer from hosted to local. With the local tokenizer the response no longer includes token_strings. The model parameter also became required (previously optional). Pass offline=False to restore the old hosted-tokenizer behavior and token_strings field.

changes.before:
co_v1.chat(
    message="who won euro 2024",
    connectors=[{"id": "web-search"}],
)
# or: search_queries_only=True, prompt_truncation="AUTO", conversation_id=..., citation_quality="fast"
changes.after:
# connectors / search_queries_only / prompt_truncation / conversation_id are gone in v2.
# Web search is now expressed as a tool:
web_search_tool = [{"type": "function", "function": {"name": "web_search", ...}}]
co_v2.chat(model=..., messages=messages, tools=web_search_tool)
# citation_quality -> citation_options={"mode": ...}
changes.migration_note: Several v1 chat parameters have no v2 equivalent and are silently rejected: connectors (replaced by user-defined tools), search_queries_only, prompt_truncation, conversation_id (chat history is now managed entirely by the developer via messages), and force_single_step (all tool calls are multi-step by default). citation_quality is replaced by citation_options with a mode key.

entries.summary: Vertex AI SDK generative_models module (vertexai.generative_models) is deprecated as of June 24, 2025 and will be removed June 24, 2026. Must migrate to google-genai with Vertex backend.

changes.symbol_after: from google import genai; client = genai.Client(vertexai=True, ...)
changes.before:
import vertexai
vertexai.init(project="my-project", location="us-central1")
from vertexai.generative_models import GenerativeModel
model = GenerativeModel("gemini-1.5-pro")
response = model.generate_content("Hello")
changes.after:
from google import genai
client = genai.Client(
    vertexai=True,
    project="my-project",
    location="us-central1"
)
response = client.models.generate_content(
    model="gemini-2.5-flash",
    contents="Hello"
)
changes.migration_note: vertexai.generative_models is deprecated (June 24, 2025) and will be removed June 24, 2026. Install google-genai and use genai.Client(vertexai=True, project=..., location=...) to access Vertex AI backend.

changes.before:
from vertexai.language_models import ChatModel
chat_model = ChatModel.from_pretrained("chat-bison")
chat = chat_model.start_chat()
response = chat.send_message("Hello")
changes.after:
from google import genai
client = genai.Client(vertexai=True, project="my-project")
response = client.models.generate_content(
    model="gemini-2.5-flash",
    contents="Hello"
)
changes.migration_note: vertexai.language_models deprecated. Use google-genai client.models.generate_content() with Gemini models.

changes.before:
from vertexai.vision_models import ImageTextModel
model = ImageTextModel.from_pretrained("imagetext")
changes.after:
from google import genai
from google.genai import types
client = genai.Client(vertexai=True, project="my-project")
# Use generate_content with image parts
changes.migration_note: vertexai.vision_models deprecated. Use client.models.generate_content() with image parts in contents.

changes.before:
import vertexai
vertexai.init(project="my-project", location="us-central1")
changes.after:
from google import genai
client = genai.Client(
    vertexai=True,
    project="my-project",
    location="us-central1"
)
changes.migration_note: Module-level init() replaced by Client constructor with vertexai=True flag.

changes.before:
import vertexai
vertexai.init(project="my-project", location="us-central1")
changes.after:
from google import genai
client = genai.Client(vertexai=True, project="my-project", location="us-central1")
changes.migration_note: The vertexai package is deprecated. Install google-genai and use genai.Client(vertexai=True, ...) for Vertex AI backend access.

changes.symbol_before: from vertexai.generative_models import Content, Part, HarmCategory, SafetySetting
changes.before:
from vertexai.generative_models import Content, Part, HarmCategory, SafetySetting
part = Part.from_text("Hello")
content = Content(parts=[part], role="user")
changes.after:
from google.genai import types
part = types.Part.from_text(text="Hello")
content = types.Content(parts=[part], role="user")
changes.migration_note: Content, Part, HarmCategory, and SafetySetting moved to google.genai.types. Import them from the types module.

changes.before:
from vertexai.generative_models import GenerativeModel
model = GenerativeModel("gemini-1.5-pro")
response = model.generate_content("Hello")
changes.after:
response = client.models.generate_content(
    model="gemini-2.5-flash",
    contents="Hello"
)
changes.migration_note: GenerativeModel class removed. Use client.models.generate_content(model=..., contents=...) directly. Pass the model name as a parameter.

changes.before:
from vertexai.language_models import ChatModel
chat_model = ChatModel.from_pretrained("chat-bison")
chat = chat_model.start_chat()
response = chat.send_message("Hello")
changes.after:
response = client.models.generate_content(
    model="gemini-2.5-flash",
    contents="Hello"
)
changes.migration_note: ChatModel.from_pretrained() removed. PaLM chat models are deprecated. Use client.models.generate_content() with Gemini models.

changes.before:
from vertexai.language_models import TextGenerationModel
text_model = TextGenerationModel.from_pretrained("text-bison")
response = text_model.predict("Write a summary")
changes.after:
response = client.models.generate_content(
    model="gemini-2.5-flash",
    contents="Write a summary"
)
changes.migration_note: TextGenerationModel.from_pretrained() removed. PaLM text models are deprecated. Use client.models.generate_content() with Gemini models.

changes.before:
from vertexai.vision_models import ImageTextModel, Image
vision_model = ImageTextModel.from_pretrained("imagetext")
image = Image.load_from_file("photo.jpg")
captions = vision_model.get_captions(image)
changes.after:
from google.genai import types
# Upload image file and use in contents
file = client.files.upload(file="photo.jpg")
response = client.models.generate_content(
    model="gemini-2.5-flash",
    contents=[file, "Describe this image"]
)
changes.migration_note: ImageTextModel.from_pretrained() removed. Use client.models.generate_content() with image parts in contents. Upload files via client.files.upload().

changes.before:
model = GenerativeModel("gemini-1.5-pro")
response = model.generate_content("Hello, world!")
changes.after:
response = client.models.generate_content(
    model="gemini-2.5-flash",
    contents="Hello, world!"
)
changes.migration_note: model.generate_content() removed. Use client.models.generate_content(model=..., contents=...).
Streaming moved to client.models.generate_content_stream(). Same parameters as generate_content.

changes.before:
model = GenerativeModel("gemini-1.5-pro")
chat = model.start_chat()
response = chat.send_message("Hello!")
changes.after:
chat = client.chats.create(model="gemini-2.5-flash")
response = chat.send_message("Hello!")
changes.migration_note: model.start_chat() removed. Use client.chats.create(model=...) to create a chat session.

changes.before:
from vertexai.generative_models import Part
part = Part.from_text("Hello")
changes.after:
from google.genai import types
part = types.Part.from_text(text="Hello")
changes.migration_note: Part.from_text() moved to types.Part.from_text(text=...) in google.genai. The parameter is now keyword-only.

changes.before:
chat = model.start_chat()
response = chat.send_message("Hello!")
changes.after:
chat = client.chats.create(model="gemini-2.5-flash")
response = chat.send_message(message="Hello!")
changes.migration_note: chat.send_message() API changed. Use client.chats.send_message(message=...) with the new chat session API.

changes.before:
from vertexai.vision_models import Image
image = Image.load_from_file("photo.jpg")
changes.after:
# Upload the file and reference it in contents
file = client.files.upload(file="photo.jpg")

changes.before:
text_model = TextGenerationModel.from_pretrained("text-bison")
response = text_model.predict("Write a summary")
changes.after:

entries.summary: google-generativeai package is deprecated and archived. Replaced by google-genai with a completely different client-based API. Old code using genai.configure() and GenerativeModel() will break.

changes.before:
import google.generativeai as genai
genai.configure(api_key="AIza...")
changes.after:
from google import genai
client = genai.Client(api_key="AIza...")
changes.migration_note: The google-generativeai package is deprecated (archived Dec 2025). Install google-genai instead. The new SDK uses a Client instance rather than module-level configuration.

changes.before:
import google.generativeai as genai
genai.configure(api_key="AIza...")
changes.after:
from google import genai
client = genai.Client(api_key="AIza...")
changes.migration_note: Module-level configure() removed. Create a Client instance with the API key passed to the constructor.

changes.before:
import google.generativeai as genai
genai.configure(api_key="AIza...")
model = genai.GenerativeModel('gemini-pro')
response = model.generate_content("Hello")
print(response.text)
changes.after:
from google import genai
client = genai.Client(api_key="AIza...")
response = client.models.generate_content(
    model="gemini-2.5-flash",
    contents="Hello"
)
print(response.text)
changes.migration_note: GenerativeModel class removed. Use client.models.generate_content() directly with model and contents parameters.
Streaming moved to client.models.generate_content_stream(). Same parameters as generate_content.

changes.before:
from google.generativeai import caching
cache = caching.CachedContent.create(...)
changes.after:
# No separate import; use client.caches
cache = client.caches.create(...)
changes.migration_note: Caching module removed. Use client.caches directly.

changes.before:
response = model.generate_content(
    "Hello",
    generation_config=genai.types.GenerationConfig(
        temperature=0.7,
        max_output_tokens=100
    )
)
changes.after:
from google.genai import types
response = client.models.generate_content(
    model="gemini-2.5-flash",
    contents="Hello",
    config=types.GenerateContentConfig(
        temperature=0.7,
        max_output_tokens=100
    )
)
changes.migration_note: generation_config parameter renamed to config. Use types.GenerateContentConfig from google.genai.

changes.before:
from google.generativeai import types
config = types.GenerationConfig(temperature=0.7)
changes.after:
from google.genai import types
config = types.GenerateContentConfig(temperature=0.7)
changes.migration_note: Types module moved from google.generativeai to google.genai.

changes.before:
config = genai.types.GenerationConfig(
    temperature=0.7,
    max_output_tokens=100
)
changes.after:
from google.genai import types
config = types.GenerateContentConfig(
    temperature=0.7,
    max_output_tokens=100
)
changes.migration_note: GenerationConfig class renamed to types.GenerateContentConfig. Import types from google.genai.

changes.before:
model = genai.GenerativeModel('gemini-pro')
response = model.generate_content("Hello")
changes.after:
response = client.models.generate_content(
    model="gemini-2.5-flash",
    contents="Hello"
)
changes.migration_note: model.generate_content() removed. Use client.models.generate_content(model=..., contents=...). The model name is now passed as a parameter.

changes.before:
model = genai.GenerativeModel('gemini-pro')
chat = model.start_chat(history=[])
response = chat.send_message("Hello!")
changes.after:
chat = client.chats.create(model="gemini-2.5-flash")
response = chat.send_message("Hello!")

changes.before:
from google.generativeai import caching
cache = caching.CachedContent.create(
    model="gemini-pro",
    display_name="my-cache",

entries.summary: The farm-haystack package was replaced by haystack-ai for Haystack 2.x; the two cannot coexist.

changes.before: pip install farm-haystack
changes.after: pip install haystack-ai
changes.migration_note: The entire Haystack 1.x distribution package farm-haystack was replaced by haystack-ai for Haystack 2.x. The two packages cannot coexist in the same Python environment — installing both causes conflicts because the package manager treats them as the same haystack module namespace. Users must uninstall both then install only haystack-ai. The farm keyword was dropped from the package name to reflect the move away from the FARM library.

changes.before: from haystack.nodes import BM25Retriever, FARMReader, EmbeddingRetriever, DensePassageRetriever
changes.after:
from haystack.components.retrievers import InMemoryBM25Retriever
from haystack.components.retrievers.in_memory import InMemoryEmbeddingRetriever
from haystack.components.readers import ExtractiveReader
changes.migration_note: The entire haystack.nodes module was removed in Haystack 2.x. Nodes were replaced by components under haystack.components. Importing from haystack.nodes raises ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'haystack.nodes'. Each 1.x node maps to a component in a specific submodule (retrievers, readers, embedders, generators, converters, builders).

changes.before:
pipeline.add_node(component=retriever, name="Retriever", inputs=["Query"])
pipeline.add_node(component=reader, name="Reader", inputs=["Retriever"])
changes.after:
pipeline.add_component("retriever", retriever)
pipeline.add_component("reader", reader)
pipeline.connect("retriever.documents", "reader.documents")
changes.migration_note: The Pipeline.add_node() method was removed entirely in Haystack 2.x. The 1.x model of adding named nodes with explicit inputs=['Query'] / inputs=['Retriever'] connection lists is replaced by add_component(name, component) followed by connect(source.output, target.input). Connections are now made by explicit output-to-input name wiring rather than by node name references. Incompatible component connections raise PipelineConnectError.

changes.before: result = pipeline.run(query="What is machine learning?")
changes.after: result = pipeline.run({"retriever": {"query": "What is machine learning?"}})
changes.migration_note: The Pipeline.run() signature changed from accepting top-level keyword arguments (e.g. query=, params=, documents=) to accepting a single nested dictionary keyed by component name. Each component receives its inputs as a sub-dictionary. Pipeline output is likewise keyed by component name, accessed as result['reader']['answers'] instead of flat top-level keys.

changes.before:
from haystack.pipelines import ExtractiveQAPipeline

pipe = ExtractiveQAPipeline(reader, retriever)
changes.after:
from haystack import Pipeline

pipe = Pipeline()
pipe.add_component("retriever", retriever)
pipe.add_component("reader", reader)
pipe.connect("retriever.documents", "reader.documents")
changes.migration_note: The pre-built pipeline classes from haystack.pipelines (e.g. ExtractiveQAPipeline, GenerativeQAPipeline, FAQPipeline, TranslationWrapperPipeline, JoinDocuments, MostSimilarDocumentsPipeline, RootNode) were all removed in Haystack 2.x. There is no direct 1:1 replacement class; users must compose pipelines manually using the generic Pipeline class with add_component() and connect().

Custom components changed from inheriting BaseComponent to using the @component decorator on a plain class. The run() method must declare output types via @component.output_types(...) decorator and must return a plain dictionary (not a tuple of dict + output name as in 1.x). Type annotations on run() parameters are required for the pipeline's type-checking and validation.

changes.before:
from haystack.nodes import FARMReader

reader = FARMReader(model_name_or_path="deepset/roberta-base-squad2")
changes.after:
from haystack.components.readers import ExtractiveReader

reader = ExtractiveReader(model="deepset/roberta-base-squad2")
changes.migration_note: FARMReader and TransformersReader were both removed and unified into a single ExtractiveReader component. This reflects the move away from the FARM library. The constructor parameter model_name_or_path was renamed to model.

changes.before:
reader = FARMReader(model_name_or_path="deepset/roberta-base-squad2")
embedder = SentenceTransformersEmbedder(model_name="sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2")
generator = OpenAIGenerator(model_name_or_path="gpt-4")
changes.after:
reader = ExtractiveReader(model="deepset/roberta-base-squad2")
embedder = SentenceTransformersEmbedder(model="sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2")
generator = OpenAIGenerator(model="gpt-4")
changes.migration_note: Across all Embedders, Generators, Readers, and various other components, the model_name_or_path and model_name parameters were uniformly renamed to model. This is a breaking change introduced in Haystack 2.0.0-beta.5 and carried through to the stable 2.0 release.

changes.before:
from haystack.nodes import BM25Retriever

retriever = BM25Retriever(document_store=document_store, top_k=10)
changes.after:
from haystack.components.retrievers import InMemoryBM25Retriever

retriever = InMemoryBM25Retriever(document_store=document_store, top_k=10)
changes.migration_note: Generic retrievers in 1.x (e.g. BM25Retriever, EmbeddingRetriever, DensePassageRetriever) were replaced by document-store-specific retriever components in 2.x. BM25Retriever → InMemoryBM25Retriever, EmbeddingRetriever/DensePassageRetriever → InMemoryEmbeddingRetriever. Each document store now has its own specialized retriever. Retrievers are no longer generic — they are tightly coupled to a specific DocumentStore implementation.

changes.before: from haystack.document_stores import ElasticsearchDocumentStore
changes.after: from haystack.document_stores.elasticsearch import ElasticsearchDocumentStore
changes.migration_note: Document store import paths were restructured in Haystack 2.x. Instead of importing all stores from the top-level haystack.document_stores package, each store lives in its own submodule (e.g. haystack.document_stores.elasticsearch, haystack.document_stores.in_memory). The import paths of DocumentJoiner, InMemoryDocumentStore, and InMemoryEmbeddingRetriever also changed in 2.0.0-beta.5.

changes.before: document_store = ElasticsearchDocumentStore(host="localhost", username="", password="", index="document")
changes.after: document_store = ElasticsearchDocumentStore(hosts=["http://localhost:9200"], index="document")
changes.migration_note: The host (string) parameter was replaced by hosts (list of full URLs including scheme and port). The username and password parameters were removed from the constructor; authentication is now handled via the Secret type and environment variables. This applies to Elasticsearch and other document store integrations.

changes.before: document_store = WeaviateDocumentStore(host="localhost", port=8080, index="my_index", custom_schema={...})
changes.after: document_store = WeaviateDocumentStore(url="http://localhost:8080", collection_settings={"class": "Default", ...})
changes.migration_note: For Weaviate: host and port were replaced by a single url parameter. index and custom_schema were replaced by collection_settings. Several 1.x parameters (name_field, embedding_dim, recreate_index, index_type) have no direct replacement in 2.x.

changes.before: document_store.write_document(doc)
changes.after: document_store.write_documents([doc])
changes.migration_note: The singular write_document() method was removed; the 2.x DocumentStore protocol only defines write_documents() (plural), along with count_documents(), filter_documents(), and delete_documents(). All document stores in 2.x conform to this uniform protocol interface.

changes.before:
document.text  # accessing document text content

document_store = ElasticsearchDocumentStore(text_field="content")
changes.after:
document.content  # accessing document text content

document_store = ElasticsearchDocumentStore(content_field="content")
changes.migration_note: The Document.text attribute was renamed to Document.content. Correspondingly, the text_field parameter in ElasticsearchDocumentStore and Weaviate initialization was renamed to content_field. The Document.question attribute (used in FAQ search) was removed entirely with no replacement.

changes.before: pipeline.connect(connect_from="retriever", connect_to="reader")
changes.after: pipeline.connect(sender="retriever", receiver="reader")
changes.migration_note: In Haystack 2.0.0-beta.7, the keyword arguments of Pipeline.connect() were renamed: connect_from → sender and connect_to → receiver. This is a breaking change only when connect() was called with keyword arguments; the behavior of the method did not change. The canonical 2.x idiom is positional string-based connections like connect('retriever.documents', 'reader.documents').

changes.before: from haystack.nodes import URLCacheChecker
changes.after: from haystack.components.cachers import CacheChecker
changes.migration_note: URLCacheChecker was renamed to CacheChecker in Haystack 2.0.0-beta.5. The component was also generalized to work with any type of data in the DocumentStore, not just URLs.

changes.before:
answer["offset_start_in_doc"]
answer["offset_end_in_doc"]
answer["offset_start"]
answer["offset_end"]
changes.after:
answer.offsets_in_document[0].start
answer.offsets_in_document[0].end
answer.offset_in_context[0].start
answer.offset_in_context[0].end
changes.migration_note: Reader return type changed from a dictionary to an Answer object. Offset access changed from dictionary keys (offset_start_in_doc, offset_end_in_doc, offset_start, offset_end) to object attributes (offsets_in_document[0].start, etc.). This allows for multiple answer spans (e.g. TableQA). Similarly, Label.question → Label.query, Label.answer became an Answer object (not plain str), Label.document_id → Label.document.id, and Label.model_id → Label.pipeline_id.

entries.summary: LangChain v0.3 dropped Pydantic 1 support and Python 3.8. LangChain v1.0 renamed create_react_agent to create_agent, moved legacy chains/retrievers/indexes to langchain-classic, removed initialize_agent and AgentExecutor from core, replaced pre_model_hook/post_model_hook with middleware, and changed intermediate_steps tuple shape.

changes.before: from langchain_core.pydantic_v1 import BaseModel
changes.after: from pydantic import BaseModel
changes.migration_note: v0.3 upgraded to Pydantic 2 internally. The Pydantic 1 compatibility bridges langchain_core.pydantic_v1 and pydantic.v1 are removed. Use Pydantic 2 directly.

changes.before:
# Python 3.8 supported in v0.2
# setup.py / pyproject.toml: python_requires = ">=3.8"
changes.after: # Python 3.9+ required for v0.3; Python 3.10+ required for v1.0
changes.migration_note: v0.3 drops Python 3.8 support (3.9+ required). v1.0 drops Python 3.9 support (3.10+ required).

changes.after:
class MyTool(BaseTool):
    model_config = ConfigDict(arbitrary_types_allowed=True)
changes.migration_note: Subclasses of BaseTool, BaseChatModel, LLM must use Pydantic 2 conventions (model_config instead of class Config, model_rebuild() if needed).

changes.before:
from langgraph.prebuilt import create_react_agent
agent = create_react_agent(model="claude-sonnet-4-6", tools=[check_weather])
changes.after:
from langchain.agents import create_agent
agent = create_agent(model="claude-sonnet-4-6", tools=[check_weather])
changes.migration_note: v1.0 renames create_react_agent (in langgraph.prebuilt) to create_agent (in langchain.agents). Old function deprecated in LangGraph v1.0, slated for removal in v2.0.

changes.before: agent = create_react_agent(model="...", tools=..., prompt="You are a helpful assistant")
changes.after: agent = create_agent(model="...", tools=..., system_prompt="You are a helpful assistant")
changes.migration_note: The prompt parameter is renamed to system_prompt in create_agent.

changes.before: agent = create_react_agent(model=..., tools=..., pre_model_hook=custom_summarization_function)
changes.after:
from langchain.agents.middleware import SummarizationMiddleware
agent = create_agent(model=..., tools=..., middleware=[SummarizationMiddleware(model=..., trigger={"tokens": 1000})])
changes.migration_note: The pre_model_hook parameter is removed; replaced by middleware implementing a before_model method.

changes.before: agent = create_react_agent(model=..., tools=..., post_model_hook=custom_human_in_the_loop_hook)
changes.after:
from langchain.agents.middleware import HumanInTheLoopMiddleware
agent = create_agent(model=..., tools=[...], middleware=[HumanInTheLoopMiddleware(interrupt_on={...})])
changes.migration_note: The post_model_hook parameter is removed; replaced by middleware implementing an after_model method.

changes.before: from langchain.chains import LLMChain
changes.after: from langchain_classic.chains import LLMChain
changes.migration_note: v1.0 moves legacy chains (LLMChain, ConversationChain, etc.) to the separate langchain-classic package. Install with pip install langchain-classic.

changes.before: from langchain.retrievers import MultiQueryRetriever
changes.after: from langchain_classic.retrievers import MultiQueryRetriever
changes.migration_note: Retrievers moved from langchain.retrievers to langchain_classic.retrievers in v1.0.

changes.before: from langchain.indexes import ...
changes.after: from langchain_classic.indexes import ...
changes.migration_note: The indexing API moved from langchain.indexes to langchain_classic.indexes in v1.0.

changes.before: from langchain import hub
changes.after: from langchain_classic import hub
changes.migration_note: The hub module moved to langchain_classic in v1.0.

changes.before: from langchain.memory import ConversationBufferMemory
changes.after:
# use a LangGraph checkpointer with create_agent
# or: from langchain_classic.memory import ConversationBufferMemory
changes.migration_note: Legacy memory classes (ConversationBufferMemory and siblings) removed from core in v1.0, relocated to langchain-classic. Conversational memory now handled by LangGraph's checkpointer with thread_id.

changes.before:
from langchain.chat_models import ChatOpenAI
from langchain.llms import OpenAI
changes.after: from langchain_openai import ChatOpenAI
changes.migration_note: v1.0 removes provider re-exports from langchain.chat_models and langchain.llms. Use dedicated provider packages (langchain-openai, langchain-anthropic, etc.).

changes.before: text = response.text()
changes.after: text = response.text
changes.migration_note: v1.0 changes .text() on message objects from a method to a property. Existing .text() calls still work but emit a deprecation warning; will be removed in v2.0.

changes.symbol_after: AIMessage(content=...)  # use additional_kwargs for extra metadata
changes.before: msg = AIMessage(content="...", example=True)
changes.after: msg = AIMessage(content="...")

changes.before: from langchain.embeddings import CacheBackedEmbeddings
changes.after: from langchain_classic.embeddings import CacheBackedEmbeddings
changes.migration_note: Embeddings modules such as CacheBackedEmbeddings moved to langchain-classic. The streamlined langchain.embeddings now only exposes Embeddings and init_embeddings.

changes.symbol_before: from langchain.schema import HumanMessage, AIMessage, SystemMessage
changes.symbol_after: from langchain_core.messages import HumanMessage, AIMessage, SystemMessage
changes.before: from langchain.schema import HumanMessage, AIMessage, SystemMessage
changes.after: from langchain_core.messages import HumanMessage, AIMessage, SystemMessage

changes.before:
from langchain.chat_models import ChatOpenAI
llm = ChatOpenAI(model="gpt-4")

from langchain_openai import ChatOpenAI
llm = ChatOpenAI(model="gpt-4")

changes.before: from langchain.embeddings import OpenAIEmbeddings

changes.before:

from langchain_openai import ChatOpenAI
llm = ChatOpenAI(model="gpt-4")  # must specify explicitly

changes.before: from langchain.schema.document import Document

changes.migration_note: OpenAIEmbeddings moved from langchain-community to langchain-openai provider package.

changes.after: from langchain_core.utils.function_calling import convert_to_openai_function

changes.before: convert_pydantic_to_openai_function(pydantic_model)
changes.after: convert_to_openai_function(pydantic_model)

changes.after: convert_to_openai_function(func)

changes.after: convert_to_openai_function(tool)

changes.after: convert_to_openai_tool(tool)

changes.before: docs = retriever.get_relevant_documents(query)
changes.after: docs = retriever.invoke(query)

from langchain.agents import initialize_agent, AgentType
agent = initialize_agent(tools, llm, agent=AgentType.ZERO_SHOT_REACT_DESCRIPTION)

changes.after: result = chain.invoke(query)

changes.after: result = llm.invoke(text)

changes.after: result = tool.invoke(input)

changes.before:

changes.after: chain = prompt | llm
changes.migration_note: LLMChain deprecated in v0.1.17. Replace with LCEL: prompt | llm. Requires structural rewrite. See: https://python.langchain.com/v0.2/docs/versions/migrating_chains/

changes.before:
from langchain.chains import RetrievalQA
qa = RetrievalQA.from_chain_type(llm=llm, retriever=retriever)

from langchain.chains import create_retrieval_chain, create_history_aware_retriever

from langchain.agents import AgentType
agent = initialize_agent(tools, llm, agent=AgentType.ZERO_SHOT_REACT_DESCRIPTION)

from langchain.agents import create_react_agent

from langchain.agents import OpenAIFunctionsAgent
agent = OpenAIFunctionsAgent.from_llm_and_tools(llm, tools)

from langchain.agents import create_openai_functions_agent

entries.summary: LlamaIndex v0.10 split the monolithic package into llama-index-core plus hundreds of integration packages. All import paths changed. v0.11 removed ServiceContext and LLMPredictor. v0.13 removed legacy agent classes and QueryPipeline.

changes.symbol_before: from llama_index import VectorStoreIndex, SimpleDirectoryReader, ServiceContext, StorageContext
changes.symbol_after: from llama_index.core import VectorStoreIndex, SimpleDirectoryReader, Settings, StorageContext
changes.before: from llama_index import VectorStoreIndex, SimpleDirectoryReader, ServiceContext, StorageContext
changes.after: from llama_index.core import VectorStoreIndex, SimpleDirectoryReader, Settings, StorageContext
changes.migration_note: All core abstractions moved from llama_index to llama_index.core in v0.10. Install llama-index-core package.

changes.before: from llama_index.llms import OpenAI
changes.after: from llama_index.llms.openai import OpenAI
changes.migration_note: LLM integrations are now separate packages (llama-index-llms-openai, etc.). Use fully-qualified provider namespace path.

changes.before: from llama_index.vector_stores import PineconeVectorStore
changes.after: from llama_index.vector_stores.pinecone import PineconeVectorStore
changes.migration_note: Vector store integrations are now separate packages (llama-index-vector-stores-pinecone, etc.). Use fully-qualified provider path.

changes.before: from llama_hub.slack.base import SlackReader
changes.after: from llama_index.readers.slack import SlackReader
changes.migration_note: llama_hub is consolidated into llama_index.readers.<provider>. Install llama-index-readers-<provider> packages.

changes.before: from llama_index import Document
changes.after: from llama_index.core.schema import Document
changes.migration_note: Document class moved to llama_index.core.schema. Same applies to TextNode and other core schema types.

changes.before: from llama_index import Response
changes.after: from llama_index.core.response.schema import Response
changes.migration_note: Response class moved to llama_index.core.response.schema.

changes.symbol_after: # LLMPredictor removed — pass LLM instance directly to Settings or module kwargs
changes.before: from llama_index import LLMPredictor
changes.after:
# LLMPredictor removed — pass the LLM instance directly
# llm = OpenAI(model="gpt-4")
# Settings.llm = llm  or  index.as_query_engine(llm=llm)
changes.migration_note: LLMPredictor was deprecated in v0.10 and removed in v0.11. Instantiate LLM directly and assign to Settings.llm.

changes.before:
from llama_index import ServiceContext, set_global_service_context
service_context = ServiceContext.from_defaults(llm=OpenAI(), embed_model=OpenAIEmbedding())
set_global_service_context(service_context)
changes.after:
from llama_index.core import Settings
Settings.llm = OpenAI()
Settings.embed_model = OpenAIEmbedding()
changes.migration_note: ServiceContext was deprecated in v0.10 and removed in v0.11. Replaced by the global Settings object with lazy instantiation. Configure via direct attribute assignment.

changes.symbol_after: from llama_index.core.workflow import Workflow, StartEvent, StopEvent
changes.before:
from llama_index.core.query_pipeline import QueryPipeline
qp = QueryPipeline(modules={...}, verbose=True)
response = qp.run(query="...")
changes.migration_note: QueryPipeline and all component classes deprecated in v0.11, removed in v0.13. Replaced by event-driven Workflows with @step decorators.

changes.before:
from llama_index.core.agent import ReActAgent
agent = ReActAgent.from_tools([tool], llm=llm, verbose=True)
response = agent.chat("What is 6 times 7?")
changes.after:
from llama_index.core.agent.workflow import ReActAgent
agent = ReActAgent(tools=[tool], llm=llm)
response = await agent.run("What is 6 times 7?")
changes.migration_note: Old ReActAgent removed in v0.13. New ReActAgent from llama_index.core.agent.workflow uses direct instantiation (not from_tools) and async .run() (not .chat()).

changes.before:
from llama_index.core.agent import FunctionCallingAgent
agent = FunctionCallingAgent.from_tools([tool], llm=llm)
response = agent.chat("...")
changes.after:
from llama_index.core.agent.workflow import FunctionAgent
agent = FunctionAgent(tools=[tool], llm=llm)
response = await agent.run("...")
changes.migration_note: FunctionCallingAgent removed in v0.13. Replaced by FunctionAgent from llama_index.core.agent.workflow. Uses native function calling, direct instantiation, and async .run().

changes.before:
from llama_index.core.agent import AgentRunner
agent = AgentRunner(worker, verbose=True)
response = agent.chat("...")
changes.after:
from llama_index.core.agent.workflow import AgentWorkflow
workflow = AgentWorkflow(agents=[agent], root_agent="...")
response = await workflow.run("...")
changes.migration_note: AgentRunner/AgentWorker architecture removed in v0.13. Replaced by AgentWorkflow from llama_index.core.agent.workflow.

changes.before:
from llama_index.core.agent import OpenAIAgent
agent = OpenAIAgent.from_tools(tools, llm=llm)
changes.after:
from llama_index.core.agent.workflow import FunctionAgent
agent = FunctionAgent(tools=tools, llm=llm)
changes.migration_note: OpenAIAgent removed in v0.13. Migrate to FunctionAgent from llama_index.core.agent.workflow.

changes.before: response = agent.chat("What is 6 times 7?")
changes.after: response = await agent.run("What is 6 times 7?")
changes.migration_note: New workflow-based agents (FunctionAgent, ReActAgent, CodeActAgent, AgentWorkflow) only expose async .run(). No synchronous .chat() method. Refactor to async/await or wrap in asyncio.run().

changes.before: from llama_index import GPTSimpleVectorIndex
changes.after: from llama_index.core import VectorStoreIndex
changes.migration_note: GPTSimpleVectorIndex and GPTVectorStoreIndex consolidated into VectorStoreIndex. Integrate with various vector databases via the vector_store parameter.

changes.before:
from llama_index import PromptHelper
prompt_helper = PromptHelper(max_input_size=3900, num_output=512, chunk_overlap_ratio=0.1)
changes.after:
from llama_index.core import Settings
Settings.context_window = 3900
Settings.num_output = 512
changes.migration_note: max_input_size parameter renamed to context_window. PromptHelper deprecated — set context_window and num_output on Settings directly.

changes.before: chat_engine = index.as_chat_engine()
changes.after: chat_engine = index.as_chat_engine()  # now returns CondensePlusContextChatEngine
changes.migration_note: v0.13 changed default chat engine to CondensePlusContextChatEngine. Agent-based chat engines removed. Use workflow-based agents via AgentWorkflow for agent behavior.

entries.summary: Mistral AI Python SDK reorganized its client surface across v0.x→v1.x (flat methods moved under namespaced accessors, ChatMessage replaced by role-specific message types, MistralClient/MistralAsyncClient consolidated into Mistral) and v1.x→v2.x (PEP 420 namespace-package restructure relocating mistralai.client.* submodules, 42 request/response types renamed, GCP/Azure providers folded into the main package). Call sites importing the old symbols or invoking the old flat methods must be updated.

changes.before:
from mistralai import Mistral

client = Mistral(api_key="YOUR_API_KEY")
changes.after:
from mistralai.client import Mistral

client = Mistral(api_key="YOUR_API_KEY")
changes.migration_note: In v2.x the SDK moved to a PEP 420 namespace package format. The main client class was relocated into the `client` submodule. Old code importing `from mistralai import Mistral` will fail with AttributeError/ModuleNotFoundError. V2 corresponds to mistralai>=2, V1 to mistralai<2.

changes.before:
from mistralai.models import ...
from mistralai.types import ...
from mistralai.utils import ...
changes.after:
from mistralai.client.models import ...
from mistralai.client.types import ...
from mistralai.client.utils import ...
changes.migration_note: All mistralai.models, mistralai.types, and mistralai.utils submodules were relocated under mistralai.client.* as part of the v2.x namespace-package restructure. mistralai.extra (RunContext, MCPClientSTDIO, MCPClientSSE, response_format_from_pydantic_model, etc.) is unchanged.

changes.before:
from mistralai_gcp import MistralGoogleCloud

client = MistralGoogleCloud()
changes.after:
from mistralai.gcp.client import MistralGCP

client = MistralGCP()
changes.migration_note: GCP support is no longer a separate top-level package (mistralai[gcp]). In v2.x it is a namespace sub-package of mistralai, and the class was renamed from MistralGoogleCloud to MistralGCP. Authentication is now handled automatically via google.auth.default(); region defaults to europe-west4.

changes.before:
from mistralai.azure.client import MistralAzure

client = MistralAzure(
    azure_endpoint=os.environ["AZUREAI_ENDPOINT"],
    azure_api_key=os.environ["AZUREAI_API_KEY"],
)
changes.after:
from mistralai.azure.client import MistralAzure

client = MistralAzure(
    server_url=os.environ["AZUREAI_ENDPOINT"],
    api_key=os.environ["AZUREAI_API_KEY"],
)
changes.migration_note: Azure support moved from the separate mistralai-azure package to from mistralai.azure.client import MistralAzure. The constructor parameters were renamed: azure_endpoint= → server_url= and azure_api_key= → api_key= to align with the unified SDK surface.

changes.before:
response = client.chat(
    messages=[...],
    model="mistral-large-latest",
)
changes.after:
response = client.chat.complete(
    messages=[...],
    model="mistral-large-latest",
)
changes.migration_note: v0.x→v1.x: the flat client.chat method was reorganized under a namespaced client.chat.complete accessor. The same restructuring applied to many other endpoints (see related entries).

v0.x→v1.x: client.chat_stream became client.chat.stream. The streaming chunk structure also changed — content is now accessed via chunk.data.choices[0].delta.content rather than chunk.choices[0].delta.content.

changes.before:
client.embeddings(...)
client.completions(...)
client.completions_stream(...)
client.list_models(...)
client.files.create(...)
client.jobs.create(...)
client.jobs.retrieve(...)
changes.after:
client.embeddings.create(...)
client.fim.complete(...)
client.fim.stream(...)
client.models.list(...)
client.files.upload(...)
client.fine_tuning.jobs.create(...)
client.fine_tuning.jobs.get(...)
changes.migration_note: v0.x→v1.x reorganized many flat methods into namespaced accessors. Notably client.files.create → client.files.upload, client.completions → client.fim.complete, client.completions_stream → client.fim.stream, client.list_models → client.models.list, and the fine-tuning client.jobs.* methods moved under client.fine_tuning.jobs.* (with retrieve renamed to get).

changes.before:
from mistralai.models import ChatMessage

msg = ChatMessage(role="user", content="Hello")
changes.after:
from mistralai.models import UserMessage

msg = UserMessage(content="Hello")
changes.migration_note: v0.x→v1.x: the generic ChatMessage class was removed and replaced with role-specific message types (UserMessage, AssistantMessage, SystemMessage, ToolMessage, etc.). The role field is no longer set manually — it is implied by the message class.

changes.before:
from mistralai import MistralClient, MistralAsyncClient

client = MistralClient(api_key="YOUR_API_KEY")
async_client = MistralAsyncClient(api_key="YOUR_API_KEY")
changes.after:
from mistralai import Mistral

client = Mistral(api_key="YOUR_API_KEY")
# async usage: await client.chat.complete_async(...)
changes.migration_note: v0.x→v1.x: MistralClient and MistralAsyncClient were consolidated into a single unified Mistral client class (sync and async methods are exposed on the same class).

changes.symbol_before: from mistralai.models import AgentCreationRequest, BatchJobOut, UploadFileOut, Tools
changes.symbol_after: from mistralai.client.models import CreateAgentRequest, BatchJob, UploadFileResponse, ConversationRequestTool
changes.before: from mistralai.models import AgentCreationRequest, BatchJobIn, BatchJobOut, UploadFileOut, ListFilesOut, DeleteFileOut, JobIn, JobsOut, Tools
changes.after: from mistralai.client.models import CreateAgentRequest, CreateBatchJobRequest, BatchJob, UploadFileResponse, ListFilesResponse, DeleteFileResponse, CreateFineTuningJobRequest, ListFineTuningJobsResponse, ConversationRequestTool
changes.migration_note: v1.x→v2.x: 42 request/response types were renamed to a consistent {Verb}{Entity}Request / {Verb}{Entity}Response / {Entity} naming convention (e.g. AgentCreationRequest→CreateAgentRequest, BatchJobOut→BatchJob, UploadFileOut→UploadFileResponse). The user-facing Tools type was renamed to ConversationRequestTool. Full mapping table in MIGRATION.md.

changes.before:
from mistralai.models import FunctionTool

tool = FunctionTool(function=..., type=None)  # type was Optional[FunctionToolType]
changes.after:
from mistralai.models import FunctionTool

tool = FunctionTool(function=..., type="function")  # type is now Literal["function"]
changes.migration_note: v1.x→v2.x: FunctionTool.type changed from Optional[FunctionToolType] to Literal["function"]. Functionally equivalent if type is omitted, but explicit type-checks against the old optional type will break. v2.x enums also now accept unknown values and discriminated unions carry an Unknown variant for forward compatibility with API changes.

changes.symbol_after: (removed — use the workflows execution streaming surface)
changes.before:
client.workflows.events.send_event(...)
client.workflows.events.send_events_batch(...)
client.events.send_event(...)
client.events.send_events_batch(...)
changes.after:
# These methods were removed in v2.2.0; use the workflows execution streaming surface instead
# e.g. client.workflows.stream(...) / client.workflows.run(...)
changes.migration_note: v2.2.0 removed mistral.workflows.events.send_event, send_events_batch, mistral.events.send_event, and send_events_batch. Workflow event submission was consolidated; existing callers must migrate to the surviving workflows execution streaming API.

changes.before:
client.search_indexes.document_lookup(...)
client.search_indexes.documents_fetch(...)
client.search_indexes.generate_index_summary(...)
client.search_indexes.get_index_detail(...)
client.search_indexes.get_index_schema_file(...)
changes.after:
# v2.9.0 collapsed 15 search_indexes operations down to 4; survivors renamed in v2.9.1
client.search_indexes.register_deployment(...)
client.search_indexes.get_deployment_summaries(...)
changes.migration_note: v2.9.0 removed 12 of 15 search-index operations (document_lookup, documents_fetch, generate_index_summary, generate_schema_summary, get_index_detail, get_index_schema_detail, get_index_schema_file, get_index_summaries, get_index_summary, get_schema_summary, set_index_summary, set_schema_summary). v2.9.1 then renamed the four survivors into 'deployment' vocabulary. The index concept is being migrated, not simply deleted.

entries.summary: OpenAI Python SDK v1.0 replaced all module-level API calls with client-based APIs. Every call site must be updated.

changes.before:
import openai
openai.api_key = "sk-..."
response = openai.ChatCompletion.create(
    model="gpt-4",
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Hello"}]
)
changes.after:
from openai import OpenAI
client = OpenAI(api_key="sk-...")
response = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="gpt-4",
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Hello"}]
)
changes.migration_note: Instantiate an OpenAI() client and call client.chat.completions.create(). The api_key is passed to the client constructor, not set as a module-level variable.

changes.before:
import openai
response = openai.Completion.create(
    model="text-davinci-003",
    prompt="Hello world"
)
changes.after:
from openai import OpenAI
client = OpenAI()
response = client.completions.create(
    model="gpt-3.5-turbo-instruct",
    prompt="Hello world"
)
changes.migration_note: Use client.completions.create(). Note: text-davinci-003 model was also deprecated.

changes.before:
import openai
response = openai.Embedding.create(
    model="text-embedding-ada-002",
    input="Hello world"
)
changes.after:
from openai import OpenAI
client = OpenAI()
response = client.embeddings.create(
    model="text-embedding-ada-002",
    input="Hello world"
)
changes.migration_note: Use client.embeddings.create(). Response structure also changed — access embeddings via response.data[0].embedding.

changes.before:
import openai
response = openai.Image.create(
    prompt="A cat",
    n=1,
    size="1024x1024"
)
changes.after:
from openai import OpenAI
client = OpenAI()
response = client.images.generate(
    prompt="A cat",
    n=1,
    size="1024x1024"
)
changes.migration_note: Use client.images.generate(). Also: client.images.edit() and client.images.create_variation().

changes.before:
import openai
openai.api_key = "sk-..."
changes.after:
from openai import OpenAI
client = OpenAI(api_key="sk-...")
changes.migration_note: API key is now passed to the client constructor. The OPENAI_API_KEY environment variable is still auto-detected.
Error classes moved from openai.error module to top-level openai package. Import them directly.

changes.before:
from openai.embeddings_utils import get_embedding, cosine_similarity
embedding = get_embedding("text", engine="text-embedding-ada-002")
sim = cosine_similarity(emb1, emb2)
changes.after:
from openai import OpenAI
import numpy as np
client = OpenAI()
response = client.embeddings.create(input="text", model="text-embedding-ada-002")
embedding = response.data[0].embedding
sim = np.dot(emb1, emb2)  # cosine similarity manually
changes.migration_note: embeddings_utils.py was removed. Use client.embeddings.create() for embeddings and compute cosine similarity manually with numpy.
