entries.summary: Pinecone Python SDK v3 replaced the module-level global API (pinecone.init() + pinecone.Index()) with an object-oriented Pinecone() client class, introduced the spec parameter for index creation, and reshaped the upsert/query data-plane APIs.

changes.symbol_after: from pinecone import Pinecone; pc = Pinecone(api_key=...)
changes.before:
import pinecone
pinecone.init(api_key="YOUR_API_KEY", environment="us-west1-gcp")
changes.after:
from pinecone import Pinecone
pc = Pinecone(api_key="YOUR_API_KEY")
changes.migration_note: The global pinecone.init() function was removed entirely. The new entry point is the Pinecone client class. No compatibility shim; calling pinecone.init() raises AttributeError in v3.

changes.before: pinecone.init(api_key="YOUR_API_KEY", environment="us-west1-gcp")
changes.after: pc = Pinecone(api_key="YOUR_API_KEY")
changes.migration_note: The environment parameter was removed from client initialization. Cloud/region is now chosen per-index via the spec parameter at index creation time.

changes.before: os.environ['PINECONE_ENVIRONMENT'] = 'us-west1-gcp'
changes.after: os.environ['PINECONE_API_KEY'] = 'YOUR_API_KEY'
changes.migration_note: PINECONE_ENVIRONMENT environment variable removed. Only PINECONE_API_KEY is needed. Environment is specified per-index through ServerlessSpec or PodSpec.

changes.before: pinecone.create_index(name="my-index", dimension=1536)
changes.after:
from pinecone import Pinecone, ServerlessSpec
pc = Pinecone(api_key="YOUR_API_KEY")
pc.create_index(name="my-index", dimension=1536, metric="cosine", spec=ServerlessSpec(cloud="aws", region="us-east-1"))
changes.migration_note: The spec parameter is now required on create_index(). Must pass ServerlessSpec(cloud, region) or PodSpec(environment, pod_type).

changes.before: pinecone.create_index(name="my-index", dimension=1536, index_type=..., index_config=...)
changes.after: pc.create_index(name="my-index", dimension=1536, spec=ServerlessSpec(cloud="aws", region="us-east-1"))
changes.migration_note: index_type and index_config parameters removed from create_index(). Index-type configuration is now expressed through the spec object.

changes.before: index = pinecone.Index("my-index")
changes.after:
pc = Pinecone(api_key="YOUR_API_KEY")
index = pc.Index("my-index")
changes.migration_note: Index() moved from a module-level function to an instance method on the Pinecone client. Must be called on a Pinecone instance.

changes.before:
pinecone.list_indexes()
pinecone.delete_index("my-index")
pinecone.describe_index("my-index")
changes.after:
pc.list_indexes()
pc.delete_index("my-index")
pc.describe_index("my-index")
changes.migration_note: All control-plane operations moved from module-level functions to instance methods on the Pinecone client object.

changes.before: index.upsert([("vec1", [0.1, 0.2, 0.3], {"genre": "drama"})])
changes.after: index.upsert(vectors=[{"id": "vec1", "values": [0.1, 0.2, 0.3], "metadata": {"genre": "drama"}}])
changes.migration_note: The vector list must now be passed as the named keyword argument vectors= rather than positionally. v3 accepts dicts, Vector objects, and tuples.
Query response changed from dict-like object to typed object with attribute access. Use response.matches and match.id instead of dict-style indexing.

changes.before:
pip install pinecone-client
import pinecone
changes.after:
pip install pinecone
from pinecone import Pinecone
changes.migration_note: Package name renamed from pinecone-client to pinecone (enforced from v6.0.0). Remove pinecone-client from dependencies and add pinecone.

entries.summary: HuggingFace Transformers v5 removes TensorFlow and JAX/Flax backends entirely (PyTorch only), removes deprecated FeatureExtractor in favor of ImageProcessor, replaces use_auth_token with token, and requires quantization_config instead of load_in_4bit/load_in_8bit.

changes.before:
from transformers import TFAutoModel
model = TFAutoModel.from_pretrained("bert-base-uncased")

from transformers import TFBertModel
model = TFBertModel.from_pretrained("bert-base-uncased")

from transformers import FlaxAutoModel
model = FlaxAutoModel.from_pretrained("bert-base-uncased")
changes.after:
from transformers import AutoModel
model = AutoModel.from_pretrained("bert-base-uncased")

from transformers import BertModel
model = BertModel.from_pretrained("bert-base-uncased")
changes.migration_note: TensorFlow and JAX/Flax model classes removed in v5. PyTorch is the sole backend. Migrate all TF/Flax code to PyTorch equivalents.

changes.before: model = AutoModel.from_pretrained("model_name", use_auth_token="hf_...")
changes.after: model = AutoModel.from_pretrained("model_name", token="hf_...")
changes.migration_note: use_auth_token parameter removed. Use token= instead.

changes.before:
model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(
    "meta-llama/Llama-3.2-3B",
    load_in_4bit=True
)
changes.after:
from transformers import BitsAndBytesConfig
quantization_config = BitsAndBytesConfig(load_in_4bit=True)
model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(
    "meta-llama/Llama-3.2-3B",
    quantization_config=quantization_config
)
changes.migration_note: Direct load_in_4bit/load_in_8bit parameters removed. Use BitsAndBytesConfig with quantization_config.

changes.before:
from transformers import AutoFeatureExtractor
extractor = AutoFeatureExtractor.from_pretrained("model")
changes.after:
from transformers import AutoImageProcessor
processor = AutoImageProcessor.from_pretrained("model")
changes.migration_note: FeatureExtractor classes deprecated and removed. Use AutoImageProcessor instead.

changes.before:
from transformers import AutoModelWithLMHead
model = AutoModelWithLMHead.from_pretrained("gpt2")
changes.after:
# For causal LM (GPT, Llama, etc.):
from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM
model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained("gpt2")

# For masked LM (BERT, RoBERTa, etc.):
from transformers import AutoModelForMaskedLM

# For encoder-decoder (T5, BART, etc.):
from transformers import AutoModelForSeq2SeqLM
changes.migration_note: AutoModelWithLMHead removed. Use AutoModelForCausalLM, AutoModelForMaskedLM, or AutoModelForSeq2SeqLM depending on model type.

changes.before:
trainer = Trainer(
    model=model,
    tokenizer=tokenizer,
    args=training_args,
    train_dataset=dataset
)
changes.after:
trainer = Trainer(
    model=model,
    processor=processor,
    args=training_args,
    train_dataset=dataset
)
changes.migration_note: Trainer's tokenizer parameter renamed to processor. Pass your tokenizer/processor as processor=.

changes.before:
# Environment variable
TRANSFORMERS_CACHE=/path/to/cache
changes.after:
# Environment variable
HF_HOME=/path/to/cache
changes.migration_note: TRANSFORMERS_CACHE environment variable replaced by HF_HOME.

entries.summary: Weaviate Python client v4 is a complete API rewrite. The v3 weaviate.Client class is removed, replaced by connection helpers and WeaviateClient. Schema/class API replaced by collections API. GraphQL query builder replaced by collection.query methods. All responses now return typed objects instead of raw dicts.

changes.before:
import weaviate
client = weaviate.Client(url="http://localhost:8080")
changes.after:
import weaviate
client = weaviate.connect_to_local()
# or: client = weaviate.WeaviateClient(connection_params=...); client.connect()
changes.migration_note: The v3 weaviate.Client class is removed. v4 replaces it with connection-helper functions (connect_to_local, connect_to_weaviate_cloud, connect_to_embedded) and the new WeaviateClient class.

changes.before:
client = weaviate.Client(url="http://localhost:8080")
# ... use client ...
# (no close needed)
changes.after:
client = weaviate.connect_to_local()
try:
    # ... use client ...
    pass
finally:
    client.close()
# or: with weaviate.connect_to_local() as client: ...
changes.migration_note: v4 client connections must be explicitly closed with client.close() or managed via a context manager. Required because v4 maintains a persistent gRPC connection.

changes.after:
from weaviate.classes.config import Property, DataType
client.collections.create(
    "Article",
    properties=[Property(name="title", data_type=DataType.TEXT)],
)
changes.migration_note: v3's client.schema.create_class() (dict-based schema API) replaced by client.collections.create() with typed Property and DataType classes. A 'Class' is now a 'Collection'.

changes.before: client.data_object.create({"question": "..."}, "JeopardyQuestion")
changes.after:
questions = client.collections.use("JeopardyQuestion")
new_uuid = questions.data.insert(properties={"question": "..."})
changes.migration_note: v3 client.data_object.create() removed. v4 requires obtaining the collection first via client.collections.use(name), then calling collection.data.insert().

changes.before:
result = (
    client.query.get("JeopardyQuestion", ["question"])
    .with_near_text({"concepts": ["animal"]})
    .with_limit(2)
    .do()
)
changes.after:
questions = client.collections.use("JeopardyQuestion")
response = questions.query.near_text(query="animal", limit=2)
for o in response.objects:
    print(o.properties)
changes.migration_note: v3's GraphQL builder pattern removed. v4 exposes query methods (near_text, hybrid, bm25, fetch_objects) directly on collection.query, returning typed objects via response.objects.

changes.before:
result = client.query.get("Article", ["title"]).do()
title = result["data"]["Get"]["Article"][0]["title"]
changes.migration_note: v4 parses responses into typed custom-class instances rather than returning raw dicts. Each object exposes .properties, .uuid, .references, .vector, and .metadata attributes.

changes.before:
with client.batch as batch:
    batch.add_data_object({"title": "..."}, "Article")
changes.after:
with client.batch.dynamic() as batch:
    batch.add_object(properties={"title": "..."}, collection="Article")
changes.migration_note: v4 removed the implicit 'with client.batch as batch' form. Must use explicit algorithm context managers: dynamic() (recommended), fixed_size(), or rate_limit().

changes.before:
from weaviate import Filter
Filter(path="round")
FilterMetadata.ByXX
changes.after:
from weaviate.classes.query import Filter
Filter.by_property(name="round")
Filter.by_id()
Filter.by_creation_time()
Filter.by_update_time()
changes.migration_note: Filter API rewritten. Filter(path=...) replaced by explicit builders (by_property, by_ref, by_id). FilterMetadata.ByXX replaced by Filter.by_id(), Filter.by_creation_time(), Filter.by_update_time().

changes.before:
client.batch.add_reference(
    from_object_uuid=src_uuid,
    from_object_collection="WikiArticle",
    from_property_name="linkedArticle",
    to_object_uuid=tgt_uuid,
)
changes.after:
batch.add_reference(
    from_uuid=src_uuid,
    from_collection="WikiArticle",
    from_property="linkedArticle",
    to=tgt_uuid,
)
changes.migration_note: Batch reference parameters renamed: from_object_uuid to from_uuid, from_object_collection to from_collection, from_property_name to from_property, to_object_uuid to to (now accepts single UUID or list).

changes.before:
vectorizer_config=...
vectorize_class_name=True
vector_index_type="hnsw"
quantitizer=...
changes.after:
vector_config=...
vectorize_collection_name=True
# vector_index_type removed — use Configure.VectorIndex.hnsw(...)
quantizer=...
changes.migration_note: Parameter renames: vectorizer_config to vector_config, vectorize_class_name to vectorize_collection_name, vector_index_type removed (use Configure.VectorIndex.hnsw()), misspelled quantitizer corrected to quantizer.

changes.before:
collection.data.reference_add(ref=target_uuid, ...)
FromReference(...)
changes.after:
collection.data.reference_add(to=target_uuid, ...)
QueryReference(...)
changes.migration_note: The ref keyword for reference operations renamed to to. DataReferenceOneToMany merged into DataReference. FromReference renamed to QueryReference.

changes.before:
obj.metadata.uuid
obj.metadata.creation_time_unix
obj.metadata.last_update_time_unix
changes.after:
obj.uuid
obj.metadata.creation_time  # datetime
obj.metadata.last_update_time  # datetime
changes.migration_note: metadata.uuid moved to top-level object.uuid. creation_time_unix renamed to metadata.creation_time (now returns datetime). last_update_time_unix renamed to metadata.last_update_time.

changes.before:
# v3: only HTTP port 8080 needed
client = weaviate.Client(url="http://localhost:8080")
changes.after:
# v4: requires gRPC port 50051 in addition to HTTP port 8080
client = weaviate.connect_to_local()
changes.migration_note: v4 uses gRPC by default (port 50051) for query and batch operations. The gRPC port must be open and reachable. Requires Weaviate server >= 1.23.7.

entries.summary: Anthropic TypeScript SDK migrated from node-fetch to builtin global fetch, removed web shims, dropped EOL Node.js versions, removed countTokens from Bedrock/Vertex clients, and removed Stream.toReadableStream(). Legacy model types also removed across versions.

changes.before: import Anthropic from 'anthropic';
changes.after: import Anthropic from '@anthropic-ai/sdk';
changes.migration_note: The default import path was renamed from the bare 'anthropic' specifier to the scoped '@anthropic-ai/sdk' package name (TypeScript SDK 0.20+). package.json must also be updated.

changes.before: const readable = stream.toReadableStream();
changes.after:
// use async iterator: for await (const event of stream) { ... }
// or use stream.withResponse() for raw access
changes.migration_note: Stream.toReadableStream() was removed in v0.20.0. Use the stream's async iterator or the .withResponse() helper added in v0.35.0.

changes.before: const count = await anthropicVertex.countTokens({ model: '...', messages: [...] });
changes.after: // use client.messages.countTokens() or client.beta.messages.countTokens()
changes.migration_note: In v0.33.0 the unsupported countTokens method was removed from both Bedrock and Vertex clients. Use messages.countTokens or beta.messages.countTokens instead.

changes.symbol_after: # shims no longer needed; SDK uses global fetch
changes.migration_note: v0.34+ migrated from node-fetch to built-in global fetch. Web shims no longer needed (will error if multiple SDK versions present). httpAgent option no longer works — proxying must be done via a custom fetch option.

changes.symbol_before: # SDK ran on older Node.js versions including EOL releases
changes.before:
// SDK ran on Node.js 16 or older
// package.json: "engines": { "node": ">=16" }
changes.after: // requires Node.js 18+ (non-EOL)
changes.migration_note: v0.50.0 dropped support for end-of-life Node.js versions. Combined with the builtin-fetch migration (requires Node 18+), projects on Node 16 or older must upgrade.

changes.before: const msg = await client.messages.create({ model: 'claude-instant-1.2', max_tokens: 1024, messages: [...] });
changes.after: // use current model identifiers (claude-sonnet-4-6, claude-opus-4-1, etc.)
changes.migration_note: Legacy model identifiers removed/deprecated across versions: claude-instant-1.2 removed in v0.33.0, claude-1 models deprecated in v0.27.2, older deprecated models removed in v0.58.0.

entries.summary: @google/generative-ai npm package is deprecated. Replaced by @google/genai with a different client class, method signatures, and removed enum imports.

changes.before:
import { GoogleGenerativeAI } from "@google/generative-ai";
const genAI = new GoogleGenerativeAI("AIza...");
changes.after:
import { GoogleGenAI } from "@google/genai";
const ai = new GoogleGenAI({ apiKey: "AIza..." });
changes.migration_note: Package renamed. Install @google/genai. GoogleGenerativeAI class replaced by GoogleGenAI. API key passed as object property.
getGenerativeModel() removed. Use ai.models.generateContent() directly with model and contents.
HarmCategory and HarmBlockThreshold enums removed. Use string values directly in config.safetySettings.

changes.before:
import { GoogleGenerativeAI, SchemaType } from "@google/generative-ai";
const schema = { type: SchemaType.OBJECT, properties: { ... } };
changes.after:
import { GoogleGenAI } from "@google/genai";
const schema = { type: "object", properties: { ... } };
changes.migration_note: SchemaType enum removed. Use string values like 'array', 'object', 'string' directly.
GoogleAIFileManager and GoogleAICacheManager removed. Use ai.files and ai.caches on the GoogleGenAI client instance.

entries.summary: OpenAI Node.js SDK v4 replaced module-level API calls with client-based APIs, matching the Python v1.0 rewrite.

changes.migration_note: Configuration and OpenAIApi classes removed. Use new OpenAI() client. Methods are now nested: openai.chat.completions.create() instead of openai.createChatCompletion().
Use openai.completions.create(). Note: text-davinci-003 model was also deprecated.
Use openai.embeddings.create().
Use openai.images.generate(). Also: openai.images.edit() and openai.images.createVariation().

changes.before:
// v3: response wrapped in .data
const content = response.data.choices[0].message.content;
changes.after:
// v4: response is direct
const content = response.choices[0].message.content;
changes.migration_note: Response objects no longer wrapped in .data. Access response.choices directly.

entries.summary: Vercel AI SDK v7 requires Node.js 22+, ESM imports only (no CommonJS), and moves OpenTelemetry to a separate package.

changes.before:
// v6: CommonJS require() worked
const { generateText } = require("ai");
changes.after:
// v7: ESM imports required
import { generateText } from "ai";
changes.migration_note: AI SDK 7 requires ESM imports. Add type module to package.json or use .mjs file extensions. CommonJS require() is not supported.
Node.js 22 is the minimum. The SDK depends on native fetch and improved AsyncLocalStorage APIs not available in earlier LTS versions. Update your runtime and CI environments.

changes.before:
// v6: OpenTelemetry setup was inline
import { generateText, experimental_telemetry } from "ai";
changes.migration_note: OpenTelemetry setup moved to @ai-sdk/otel package. Register telemetry globally instead of per-call.

entries.summary: Vercel AI SDK v6 changed message structure from flat content strings to typed parts arrays, renamed Experimental_Agent to ToolLoopAgent, and changed agent parameters.

changes.migration_note: Messages no longer carry a flat content string. They carry a parts array of typed entries. Rewrite every component that renders message.content.

changes.before:
import { Experimental_Agent } from "ai";
const agent = new Experimental_Agent({ ... });
changes.after:
import { ToolLoopAgent } from "ai";
const agent = new ToolLoopAgent({ ... });
changes.migration_note: Experimental_Agent replaced by ToolLoopAgent.
The 'system' parameter is renamed to 'instructions'.
Default stopWhen changed from 1 step to 20 steps. Set stopWhen: 1 explicitly to restore old behavior.
